findings.finding: Scientific consultant Darren Naish describes using crocodilian/bird comparisons and lowering recorded large-bird calls to create varied resonant animal voices for Prehistoric Planet.
findings.applied: Keep recognizable recorded vocal articulation; use restrained pitch changes and separate roar, grunt, bellow and squawk families.

findings.finding: Museum expert interview distinguishes closed-mouth animal booms/growls from cinematic roars; film effects are composites of existing animal recordings.
findings.applied: T-Rex and Spinosaurus are clearly labeled cinematic designs, with a recorded growl layer; these are not claimed as exact scientific reconstructions.

findings.finding: CT-based Parasaurolophus crest modeling supports possible low resonant tones; missing soft tissue means the reconstruction is approximate.
findings.applied: A stylized horn family instead of assigning the same roar to this dinosaur. Our audible horn is original synthesis, not Sandia audio or a replicated crest model.
